page: Amazon Web Services c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. The instance provides 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not included, and the instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between CPU and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; PassMark memory benchmarks place the instance in the bottom 10%, and both cached and uncached memory bandwidth read and write tests rank in the bottom 25%. This performance profile is reflected in weak multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6a.xlarge offers dedicated compute resources at a lower entry point within the compute-optimized class, but the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak memory bandwidth limit its efficiency for memory-bound workloads. It is appropriate for compute-bound tasks that require strong single-core performance but have low memory footprints, such as single-threaded compression, basic web serving, or lightweight text processing. It is less recommended for memory-intensive databases or complex multi-threaded compilation.
